checks.what: mughal-empire keyframes 1659-1741 (with the 1740 split) now subtract Ratnapura's 1114 shape. That is 257 cells (Chhattisgarh 241, Madhya Pradesh 16), the same as kalachuris-of-ratnapura's own 1114 and 1740 shapes, and no other land is removed. The Chhattisgarh page says the Ratanpur/Raipur rulers 'acknowledged the nominal overlordship of the Mughals when they arrived'. The Kalachuris_of_Ratnapura page does not mention the Mughals and says the kingdom 'accepted the suzerainty of the Maratha Nagpur Kingdom in 1740'.

Garhwal's 1358 shape (101 cells) is out of the Mughal keyframes 1588-1756. Mughal 1757-1768 keep only the 2 Dun cells, matching garhwal-kingdom's 1757 shape. The page infobox says 'Tributary of the Mughal Empire (1655 onwards)'. Rani Karnavati 'repelled an attack of Mughal army led by Najabat Khan in 1640'. Najib-ud-daula captured Dehradun in 1757, and the Garhwalis recovered the Dun in 1770. One small slip: the Mughal 1769 keyframe subtracts the 1770 shape, so the 2 Dun cells belong to no one in 1769. This is not worth an edit.

Each Mughal keyframe from 1588 to 1769 now misses Kumaon's shape for its start year: 73 to 94 cells of hills, Doti and Terai. Overlap remains only in 1662 (21 Terai cells) and 1741 (7 cells), as the fixer reported. The page infobox calls Kumaon a 'Vassal state of the Mughal Empire within the Subah of Delhi (16th century onwards)' and says it 'mostly remained independent and sovereign but maintained a tributary relationship'. A vassal is not Mughal land, so the subtraction is right. The hierarchy.csv handoff for kumaon-kingdom and garhwal-kingdom under mughal-empire is supported.

The 31 Mughal keyframes 1579-1741 subtract 83 cells, identical to cutch-state's 1549 shape. No Mughal keyframe still overlaps Kutch. The Cutch_State page has the 1719 invasion by the Mughal viceroy of Gujarat ending with the 'Mughal army was defeated'. It does not mention tribute, a vassal tie or Mughal rule.

The keyframe overlaps with afsharid-iran after the change are 51 cells in 1738 (Ghazni 40, K.P. 9, F.A.T.A. 2) and none in 1740, 1741 or 1744. The Mughal 1741 keyframe gains 456 cells of Pakistani Punjab, Islamabad and Azad Kashmir east of the Indus; its polygon follows the river from Attock to the Sindh border. afsharid-iran's 1741 and 1744 keyframes lose the same land. The page infobox says 'Nader Shah annexes all lands west of the Indus river'. On leaving Delhi on 16 May 1739 he 'ceded back all territories to the east of the Indus, which he had overrun, to Muhammad Shah'. It also has 'captured Kandahar' from Hussain Hotak, but the page gives no year for that. The split of the 1738 keyframe (now 1738-1739) and the new 1740 keyframe are valid; the compiler reads from and to.

The 140 km disc taken from the Mughal keyframes 1526-1564 and from ledger 0, 1, 4 and 28 is exactly bikaner-state's shape (232 cells). No other land is removed. The page lists Rao Kalyan Mal (1542-1571) as the ruler who 'acknowledged the suzerainty of Emperor Akbar'. It shows no Mughal tie before him, so the change is supported. Keeping 1741-1757 unchanged is reasonable.
The skip holds: data/hierarchy.csv row 239 has kingdom-of-mewar as a vassal of mughal-empire for 1708-1739 (confidence 1).

The Mughal keyframes no longer overlap admin-1 Tripura (34 cells in 1670-1713). From 1670 the Chittagong Hill Tracts (17 cells) are out and the port of Chittagong (7 cells) stays in. The 1576 keyframe and ledger 38, 41 and 42 exclude Sylhet and the Chittagong disc. Sylhet (23 cells) is added to the keyframes from 1612 to 1669. The Kingdom_of_Tripura page says 'the Mughals could never penetrate the Hills territories to the east'. The Sylhet page says it 'emerged after 1612 as the Mughals' most significant imperial outpost in Bengal east of Dhaka'. The 170 km Multan disc taken from the Mughal 1526 keyframe and ledger 0 and 1 is langah-sultanate's own shape (334 cells, 325 of them in the 1526 base). The page says 'annexed in 1527 but had autonomous authority until its merger with the Mughal Empire in 1530' and 'Multan fell in 1528 after an extended siege'.
The skip holds: data/hierarchy.csv row 40 has kingdom-of-tripura as a vassal of british-raj for 1858-1947 (confidence 3).

The nawabs-of-bengal keyframes 1718-1757 and its 1717 founding region drop the Tripura hills (34 cells) and the Hill Tracts (17) and keep the port. From 1733 they no longer overlap Tripura. Tripura's new 1612 loss of Sylhet was given confidence 2, but the cited Sylhet page says 'In the 16th century, Sylhet was controlled by the Baro-Bhuiyan zamindars'. So 1612 only ends the 1490 bridge and is not a dated Tripura loss. I lowered that event (kingdom-of-tripura ledger 3) to confidence 1 and added a note. The 1666 port loss (confidence 1) is another bridge end of the same kind: History_of_Chittagong has Mrauk U holding Chittagong from 1531 until 1666. It is acceptable as an improvement on the old claim to 1764, but see problems.
